<div class="page-shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Sample size for a two-sample t test in R</h1>
  <p>Before you collect data, you decide how many subjects to recruit. In this practical, you will use the R function <code>power.t.test()</code> to calculate the sample size for a given power.</p>
</header>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Overview</h2>

Deciding how many subjects to recruit is one of the more important decisions you make when planning a study. 

If you recruit too few subjects, your study may be <strong>underpowered</strong> and you may miss a real effect. 

It's also possible to recruit too many subjects, more than the study needs to demonstrate a convincing effect, and thus waste time and money.

A power analysis is usually done before the study is conducted, to determine the sample size needed to achieve a desired level of power.

There are many kinds of power analysis for different study designs and tests. This practical introduces the idea through one common case: finding sample size for a <strong>two-sample t test</strong> using the R function `power.t.test()`.

After answering all questions, <strong>your completion code will be revealed.</strong> Enter it into the LMS to mark this practical complete.

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 1</div>

  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="a">An estimate of the sample size you need per group.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="b">Proof that the new drug works.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="c">A guarantee that your p-value will be small.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. It is a planning calculation for sample size. It does not decide the result of any single study." data-incorrect="Not quite. A power analysis estimates the sample size you need. It does not prove a result or guarantee a p-value."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>The power.t.test() function call</h2>

Below is the standard syntax for the `power.t.test()` function.

```r
power.t.test(
  delta = ...,        # difference worth detecting
  sd = ...,           # standard deviation
  sig.level = 0.05,   # false-positive rate
  power = 0.80        # chance to detect a real difference
)
```

Typically, you fill in four values and leave out `n`. That is the value R solves for.

Thx box below shows the formula for the sample size calculation. You do **not** need to memorize the formula. It is here so you can see how the four inputs fit together.

<div class="formula-panel">

$$
n \approx 2\left(\frac{\bigl(z_{1-\alpha/2} + z_{1-\beta}\bigr)\,\sigma}{\delta}\right)^2
$$

<p class="formula-note"><strong>Reading the symbols:</strong> $n$ is sample size per group; $\delta$ is <code>delta</code>; $\sigma$ is <code>sd</code>; $\alpha$ is <code>sig.level</code>; and power $= 1 - \beta$, where $\beta$ is the false-negative rate. R uses a slightly more exact calculation, but this is the usual large-sample approximation.</p>

</div>

There are four inputs. Match each one to its R argument using the dropdowns, then check your answers. (The four options are <code>delta</code>, <code>sd</code>, <code>sig.level</code>, and <code>power</code>.)

<div id="arg-match">
<table class="summary-table">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>R argument (select correct one from dropdown)</th>
      <th>Meaning</th>
      <th>Where you get it</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="delta">
          <option value="">Select one</option>
          <option value="delta">delta</option>
          <option value="sd">sd</option>
          <option value="sig.level">sig.level</option>
          <option value="power">power</option>
        </select>
      </td>
      <td>The <strong>difference between group means</strong> worth detecting. The smallest effect that would matter in practice.</td>
      <td>From the study goal: what change in the outcome would you act on?</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="sd">
          <option value="">--</option>
          <option value="delta">delta</option>
          <option value="sd">sd</option>
          <option value="sig.level">sig.level</option>
          <option value="power">power</option>
        </select>
      </td>
      <td>The <strong>standard deviation</strong> of the outcome within a group; how much subjects vary (the noise).</td>
      <td>From a pilot study, published trials in similar patients, or clinical records.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="sig.level">
          <option value="">--</option>
          <option value="delta">delta</option>
          <option value="sd">sd</option>
          <option value="sig.level">sig.level</option>
          <option value="power">power</option>
        </select>
      </td>
      <td>The <strong>significance level</strong> (α): the false-positive rate you accept.</td>
      <td>Convention; usually fixed at 0.05.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
        <select class="arg-select" data-answer="power">
          <option value="">--</option>
          <option value="delta">delta</option>
          <option value="sd">sd</option>
          <option value="sig.level">sig.level</option>
          <option value="power">power</option>
        </select>
      </td>
      <td><strong>Statistical power</strong> (1 − β): the probability of detecting the difference if it is real.</td>
      <td>Convention; usually 0.80. Use 0.90 if you want a lower chance of missing a real effect (a false negative).</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Worked example 1: blood pressure study</h2>

A team is testing a new blood pressure drug against a placebo. They would like to reduce systolic blood pressure by at least 5 mmHg; a smaller reduction would not be considered worth acting on. Previous blood pressure trials in similar patients reported a standard deviation of about 8 mmHg. The team will use a 5% significance level and wants an 80% chance of detecting a real effect if one exists.

Run the cell to find the sample size needed for each group.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code for worked example 1</h3>

```{webr-r}
power.t.test(
  delta = 5,
  sd = 8,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  power = 0.80
)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 4</div>

<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="b">5</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="c">8</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 7</div>
  <p>The researchers want to increase the probability of detecting a real effect if one exists, so they raise their target power to 90%. <script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "POWERFUL";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 7;

function shuffleArgSelectOptions() {
  document.querySelectorAll("#arg-match .arg-select").forEach((sel) => {
    const options = Array.from(sel.options);
    const placeholder = options.shift();
    options.sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5);
    sel.replaceChildren(placeholder, ...options);
    sel.selectedIndex = 0;
  });
}

document.getElementById("arg-match-check")?.addEventListener("click", () => {
  const selects = document.querySelectorAll("#arg-match .arg-select");
  const feedback = document.getElementById("arg-match-feedback");
  let allSelected = true;
  let allCorrect = true;

  selects.forEach((sel) => {
    sel.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    if (!sel.value) {
      allSelected = false;
      sel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      return;
    }
    if (sel.value === sel.dataset.answer) {
      sel.classList.add("correct-choice");
    } else {
      allCorrect = false;
      sel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
    }
  });

  feedback.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
  if (!allSelected) {
    feedback.classList.add("is-incorrect");
    feedback.textContent = "Choose an argument for every row, then check again.";
  } else if (allCorrect) {
    feedback.classList.add("is-correct");
    feedback.textContent = "All four matches are correct.";
  } else {
    feedback.classList.add("is-incorrect");
    feedback.textContent = "Not quite. Check the rows highlighted in red and try again.";
  }
});

shuffleArgSelectOptions();

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
